answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, the way a sparrow defends a single nesting spot: the stake is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. Honest agents treat the deposit as a jade bond they recover in full, while an attacker must fund each fake identity separately, so the cost grows with every sybil. The shared registry becomes an oasis where only staked agents transact, making mass fake identities economically unprofitable.
